_meta.title: Local-business discovery strategy — free-first, Google Places costed
_meta.ranking_rule: Phone-number yield above everything else, per the project brief.
_meta.recommendation: Overture Maps Places as the primary Stage 3 mechanism, portal-srbija city-iteration as the geographic sweep, APR open data as the coverage frame. Google Places rejected on licence, not price.
_meta.geographic_units_note: 145 local self-government units + 17 Belgrade city municipalities, from data/serbia-geo.json (FUZZ-6).
_meta.query_terms_note: 14 contractor + 8 store terms from the project brief; diacritic and ASCII-folded spellings collapse to one call on any normalising search endpoint.

options.name: Overture Maps Foundation — places theme
options.license_notes: Places theme contains no OpenStreetMap data and carries no ODbL share-alike obligation. Storage and redistribution permitted. Joining to OSM data may make the derivative database ODbL.
options.robots_txt: not applicable — bulk object storage, no crawling
options.pagination: not applicable — GeoParquet, queried with DuckDB httpfs
options.how_measured: DuckDB httpfs against the public S3 release, filtered to addresses[1].country='RS' inside bbox 18.8-23.1 x 42.2-46.3, then taxonomy.primary in 16 target categories OR a Serbian-name regex.
options.duplicate_risk: High against any Facebook-derived source, since ~95% of Serbian records are Meta-sourced. Dedup on normalized phone first, per the project rule.
implementation_notes: Releases from December 2025 use taxonomy.primary, not categories.primary.
Pin the release string — it is part of the S3 path.
Filter confidence >= 0.3; the contractor-side subset skews low.
Run the Serbian name regex in addition to the category filter — 61 records match only by name.

options.name: Serbian directory city-iteration (portal-srbija.com)
options.robots_txt: Allow: / — only /admin*/ and /pretraga/ disallowed. City-suffixed category pages are permitted.
options.pagination: none — each category-city page is one static response
options.how_measured: Sweep at 1 req/s with an honest project user agent over the 32 most populous units plus all 17 Belgrade city municipalities from data/serbia-geo.json; firm names extracted from h2.nazivfirme and de-duplicated.
options.corrects_prior_finding: research/sources-contractors.md (FUZZ-4) records these city pages as 'strict subsets — crawl the national page only'. Measured, they are not: the national page truncates and 48 of 108 firms appear only on a city page.
options.workaround: beograd 500s; iterate Belgrade through its 17 city municipalities instead — novi-beograd (15 firms), zemun (10), vozdovac (7), vracar (6), stari-grad (4), surcin (4) all return 200.
options.crawl_budget: 9 categories x ~162 units = ~1,458 requests, ~25 minutes at 1 req/s
options.duplicate_risk: High within the source (city pages overlap the national page); dedup on normalized phone.

options.name: Navidiku.rs category x city URLs
options.robots_txt: permissive for /firme/ listing pages; /firme/ajax and /firme/noviajax disallowed
options.verdict: The taxonomy is sparse, not a cross product. Generating city x category URLs yields mostly 404s. Enumerate from sitemap-companies-001.xml.gz (13,408 companies) instead.

options.name: APR — Registar privrednih društava, open-data API
options.robots_txt: openapi.apr.gov.rs publishes no robots.txt (HTTP 404). This is the documented open-data delivery channel, so the apr.gov.rs site-wide Disallow: / does not apply to it.
options.reopens_rejected_source: FUZZ-4 rejected APR on apr.gov.rs/robots.txt (User-agent: * / Disallow: /) and flagged licensed bulk data as a commercial conversation. For companies, that conversation is unnecessary — APR already publishes the register as open data.

options.limitation: Covers privredna drustva (DOO/AD) only. Does NOT cover preduzetnici — the sole traders the project brief names as a large share of Serbian fasaderi. /api/opendata/entrepreneurs and /api/opendata/preduzetnici both return 404, and data.gov.rs has no preduzetnici dataset. This is the single largest structural coverage gap in the project.

options.name: OpenStreetMap via Overpass API
options.license_warning: Merging OSM records into the lead database can make the derivative database ODbL and pull share-alike onto the whole export. Keep OSM-sourced records flagged by source id so the choice stays reversible.
options.robots_txt: not applicable — public API, no rate-limit fee, 2 concurrent slots
options.verdict: Store side is usable as a one-request top-up (339 phones). Contractor side is dead: 4 elements for plasterer+painter+builder, 1 phone. The whole craft census for Serbia is 697 businesses — a coverage gap, not a tagging problem, so no alternative tag rescues it. Never build a geographic sweep on OSM.

options.name: General web search result scraping (Google / Bing / DuckDuckGo)
options.robots_txt: google.com Disallow: /search; bing.com Disallow: /search; duckduckgo.com Disallow: /html and Disallow: /lite
options.requires_javascript: duckduckgo.com root ?q= form is a JavaScript SPA and returns no results without a browser; the two no-JS endpoints are the disallowed ones
options.verdict: No compliant free path exists. All three engines disallow their result pages, and the project brief commits to respecting robots.txt. Building around it with rotating proxies would contradict a standing project rule.

options.name: Brave Search API
options.storage_rights: Standard terms do NOT grant storage rights — those require a plan that explicitly includes them.
options.verdict: Usable as a URL-discovery layer only: take the URLs, discard the search results, crawl the discovered sites under their own robots.txt. Roughly one-eighth the price of a Places sweep, and unlike Places what it leads you to is storable. Requires approval under the project cost policy.

options.name: Google Places API (New) — Text Search + Place Details

free_tier.note: $200 monthly credit withdrawn 2025-03-01, replaced by per-SKU free monthly thresholds

options.phone_field_tier: Enterprise — nationalPhoneNumber, internationalPhoneNumber and websiteUri are all Enterprise field-mask fields. There is no cheap tier that returns a phone number.

call_model.unique_places_anchor: Overture finds 1,856 relevant Serbian businesses; APR holds 2,813 companies under the six core activity codes; Google additionally carries preduzetnici that neither lists.

cost_plan_b_one_step.note: More expensive, and returns phones only for the <=60 results each query can reach.

blocking_clauses.ref: Google Maps Platform Terms of Service §3.2.3(a) No Scraping
blocking_clauses.text: Customer will not export, extract, or otherwise scrape Google Maps Content for use outside the Services.

blocking_clauses.ref: Google Maps Platform Terms of Service §3.2.3(b) No Caching
blocking_clauses.text: Customer will not cache Google Maps Content except as expressly permitted under the Maps Service Specific Terms.
Customer may temporarily cache latitude and longitude values from the Places API for up to 30 consecutive calendar days, after which Customer must delete the cached latitude and longitude values.

options.verdict: Rejected, and should be recorded as rejected rather than deferred. place_id may be cached indefinitely and lat/lng for 30 days; the business name, address and above all the phone number may not be stored at all. This product is a permanent SQLite system of record holding phone numbers with a review UI and an XLSX export — every one of those is storage that §3.2.3(b) forbids and §14.3 does not excuse. Buying more quota does not fix it, because quota was never the constraint.

options.name: Scraping Google Maps directly
options.question_from_issue: Is scraping Google Maps directly the right call?
options.legal_reasoning: §3.2.3(a) No Scraping covers Google Maps Content however obtained, not just via the API, so scraping the maps front end is a more explicit violation than paying for the API — not a way around it. It puts the company's Google accounts at risk for a dataset it still could not lawfully retain.
options.engineering_reasoning: Obfuscated internal endpoints with rotating parameter names and no stability contract, behind bot detection a compliant crawler cannot defeat without the CAPTCHA-bypassing and detection-evasion the project brief prohibits. Every layout change silently breaks extraction. A permanently staffed system delivering a dataset with a legal defect.
options.alternative: Overture Maps Places — 95% Meta-sourced, CDLA-Permissive-2.0 with explicit permission to store and redistribute, a single parquet download with no crawler, and a phone number on 95% of records. On phone-yield-per-record it is at least the equal of a Google sweep, and it is the only one of the two this product is allowed to keep.

options.name: data.gov.rs — remaining datasets
options.verdict: Apart from the APR company register, no dataset on the portal is a business directory with contact data. Negative result recorded so nobody re-checks.

options.name: Foursquare Open Source Places (standalone)
options.verdict: Already inside Overture and contributes only 2,538 of Serbia's 108,740 records against Meta's 103,504. Querying it separately adds nothing. Same for Microsoft (1,258), AllThePlaces (1,064) and PinMeTo (376).

stage_3_build_order.effort: one DuckDB COPY, ~90 seconds, no crawler
one Overpass request, flagged by source for the ODbL question

revisit_triggers.yield_trigger: Fewer than 2,000 unique phone-bearing leads nationally at the end of Stage 3, OR fewer than 100 of the 145 local self-government units covered by at least one lead. Overture alone should clear both (1,752 distinct phones, 179 localities), so falling short means something upstream broke — fix that before buying anything.
revisit_triggers.coverage_trigger: Measured coverage below 60% of the 2,813 APR core-code companies in tier-1 and tier-2 municipalities after the enrichment crawler has run.
revisit_triggers.what_to_buy_if_triggered: APR licensed bulk data for the preduzetnici register — not Google. The preduzetnici gap is the one measured hole in national coverage, APR is the only source that closes it, and its licence permits exactly the storage this product needs.
revisit_triggers.google_places_trigger: None. No measurement changes the outcome. It would become viable only if Google changed §3.2.3(b) and §14.3, or if the product changed into one that displays live Google results on a Google map instead of storing leads — a different product.
